notes: Copy laid out in 14 rows; stone line numbers 1-14 fall mid-row; lines 13-14 each have a right and a left half, right read first. The 3-shaped signs (m, ẖ, s) are read by tail: ) and 3-with-short-lower-left-tail = m, bigger tail = ẖ, closed 3 = s; slms (line 3) and the first sign of mli, s?tmdese are shape guesses. '/3' groups: read so in soriyi/soreyi, q in qowi, qoqoli, pqr (each could be q or s+o; the //3 groups could also be s+y). soriyi: Griffith marks the 4 (i) sic, standing where soreyi has e. tside: the last two signs S + tailed λ could be one a (tsia). 'S///' read ye (y then e) in yetmde. Σ with long tail read p, Ʒ with long tail read k (both long-tailed, p/k trap). /ϟ with bar and /+ read te. w? in lines 4 and 7: hatched sign shaped like w. beloloa?eet?: the S2 with long tail under /ς read a, could be e + k; final dotted hook read t?. psil?oteaikete: '/' + a small hooked sign read lo?, '4S2' read a then i. to? in line 9 is a ɔ with a dot. In line 6 'yetmetl?d' the sign after t has dots on both sides.

notes: No line number 1 printed. soriyi: 4ω read ri (as in Kar. 17, where Griffith marks it sic). //3 read qo in qowi. The looped λ read d (it stands in tedḫe). Line 2: a hatched sign before the k read l?. Line 3: the first te is /← with a bar; the 3 after it could be s or m; the [.] is a hatched blob, then a gap, then a hatched te. Line 9 group: 3-topped sign with tail read k, 4-like sign read i (dikte). /3 in solkte and solkete could be q (qolkte). In line 11 a small hatched blob between e and y read [.]; the 3 before te read m? (could be ẖ or s). at?mẖe: the sign after a is a 9-shaped hook without dot, read t?. The last row (lines 12-13) stands in the field, labelled 'in field'.

reading: (1)wosi : so(2)reyi : (3)wiretey?itoqowi : p(4)elmoñye : tedḫelowi (5)sq?r k?npse trosetme : (6)te[.]ri(7)k?elowi? : (8)ant : k?npse? (9)k?noteli (10)yetmdelowi : ant : k?n(11)pse brtrl : m?telowi (12)ant : s?ni : s?d?olowi : se(13)n?te m?y?p?(14)[.][.][.][.]
notes: Line 3: y? is hatched slashes after the 4; to is ب with a dot below. Line 4: the crossed sign before ye read ñ (no loop clearly visible); pelmo- may be the title. Line 5: the right group is 3, /3, ω: read s q r, could be s s o r. k?npse (three times): a 3-topped sign with a long tail read k, then n (ℛ), then Σ with long tail read p, then se; in line 8 the se is damaged (H/// form). Line 6: hatching between te and r read as one lost sign though the formula would need none. ant: in lines 8 and 12 the a is written S and a separate long-tailed 2. brtrl and trosetme are read sign by sign; the ω with a dot in brtrl read r. Line 12: the sign with a dot before it (·3) read s?; the sign /A read d? (crossed strokes, no loop). Lines 13-14: n? is a ʌ with a dot; after te come a 3 with tail (m?), hatched slashes (y?), Σ with long tail (p?), then about four signs of hatching after (14), end lost.

notes: The copy starts at line 3: the number 3 stands alone at the top right, and the text begins at a vertical stroke (an edge or break?) through the tail of the first a; lines 1-2 are not on this copy. Row 3 also starts with a long vertical stroke after tedḫe, so the text may break off there (no final divider). ḫ? in yireḫ?ed is a ( or < shape, unlike the ⊏ of tedḫe; the line ends with a dot after the ///. In worotel?iye the /ω and /K groups are read o r and te.
